review_comment: The patch adds CSS comment removal before checking for sneaky JavaScript patterns in style attributes. Without this neutralization, comment-obfuscated patterns like 'expre/*x*/ssion(' could bypass detection and reach browsers. Ensure all CSS comment syntax (/*...*/) is stripped before any JavaScript pattern matching in style sanitization.

The code adds whitespace removal to detect obfuscated JavaScript schemes in HTML links, but this represents a security control improvement rather than a vulnerability. The function attempts to neutralize malicious URLs by removing whitespace before regex pattern matching. To strengthen this control, ensure the regex pattern covers all dangerous schemes and consider additional obfuscation detection methods beyond whitespace removal.

The added whitespace removal improves detection of obfuscated JavaScript patterns in CSS styles, addressing a potential XSS bypass via style injection. When processing untrusted HTML, ensure all style attributes and style element content pass through this detection function before being included in sanitized output. Consider also validating CSS properties against a safe subset to prevent other injection vectors beyond JavaScript expressions.
